question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

170 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) separated with less than one year of federal service in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026: 78 "other separation," 76 quit, 14 termination, and 2 transfer out. Those 170 rows carry estimated location and pay, because OPM redacted both and they were filled in from job postings. Late reports keep arriving, so this count will grow slightly. I read "this year" as the trailing twelve months to August 2026, the latest data; if you meant calendar 2026 or FY2026 to date, say so.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category`,
    `location_imputed`,
    `pay_imputed`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `length_of_service_years` < 1
)
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `breakdown_type`,
  CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS `separation_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`location_imputed`, FALSE) OR COALESCE(`pay_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_flagged_location_or_pay_imputed`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`location_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_location_imputed`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`pay_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_pay_imputed`
FROM `filtered`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'BY_SEPARATION_CATEGORY' AS `breakdown_type`,
  `separation_category`,
  COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`location_imputed`, FALSE) OR COALESCE(`pay_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_flagged_location_or_pay_imputed`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`location_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_location_imputed`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(`pay_imputed`, FALSE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `rows_pay_imputed`
FROM `filtered`
WHERE `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY `separation_category`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `breakdown_type` = 'TOTAL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, `separation_category`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

Higher-graded CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) did not separate at a higher rate over the trailing twelve months to August 2026, and the pattern across grades is not a clean gradient. Grades 13 and 14 separated at 3.2% and 3.8%, below grades 05 and 07 (10.2% and 7.7%). Grade 15 is higher at 6.6%, but that rests on 12 separations.

| Grade | Separations | Mean headcount | Separation rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 05 | 67 | 655 | 10.2% |
| 07 | 81 | 1,049 | 7.7% |
| 09 | 61 | 1,545 | 3.9% |
| 11 | 8 | 1,198 | 0.7% |
| 12 | 550 | 17,325 | 3.2% |
| 13 | 136 | 4,313 | 3.2% |
| 14 | 32 | 850 | 3.8% |
| 15 | 12 | 181 | 6.6% |

Grade 00 (7 separations on about 32 people, 21.9%) is too small to read and is left out of the table. The query found no separations coded to the 2025 deferred resignation program in any grade, so the rates with and without that wave are the same. Late reports keep arriving, so recent separations will rise slightly. I read "higher-graded" as grades 13 to 15 against grades 05 to 09, and the question as the trailing twelve-month rate to August 2026; if you meant the count of separations, grade 12 dominates that count with 550, so say so and I will rank it instead.

```sql
WITH `separations_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations_total`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_drp`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` <> 'Y' OR `drp_indicator` IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_excluding_drp`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`start_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`end_headcount` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `separations_by_grade`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `start_headcount`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `end_headcount`
)
SELECT
  `grades`.`grade`,
  COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_total`, 0) AS `separations_total`,
  COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_drp`, 0) AS `separations_drp`,
  COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_excluding_drp`, 0) AS `separations_excluding_drp`,
  COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`,
  COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`,
  try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(100.0 * COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_total`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate_pct_total`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(100.0 * COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_excluding_drp`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate_pct_excluding_drp`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(100.0 * COALESCE(`separations_by_grade`.`separations_drp`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`start_headcount`.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(`end_headcount`.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate_pct_drp`
FROM `grades`
LEFT JOIN `separations_by_grade`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `separations_by_grade`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `start_headcount`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `start_headcount`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `end_headcount`
  ON `grades`.`grade` = `end_headcount`.`grade`
ORDER BY `grades`.`grade`
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The OPM data shows 838 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) in October and November 2025, and 702 of them were quits (372 in October, 330 in November). Retirements were 136 (75 and 61), and the query returned no termination or transfer-out separations. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts can still grow slightly, though two months back they should move little.

The 838 is 272 below the 1,110 figure TSA gave Congress. The data does not show whether the gap is scope (for example, other categories or other occupations) or a different counting rule. The OPM data records separation categories, not reasons, so it cannot say whether any of these separations relate to the shutdown.

I read "left" as all separations in any category for TSA screeners in the calendar months October and November 2025; if you meant only quits, the answer is 702, and if you meant the trailing twelve-month rate, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'QUIT' THEN 'QUIT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category ILIKE 'RETIREMENT%' THEN 'RETIREMENT'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'TERMINATION'
      WHEN separation.separation_category = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'TRANSFER OUT'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS separation_category_group
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation` AS separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND separation.effective_month IN (DATE('2025-10-01'), DATE('2025-11-01'))
    AND separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.separation_category IS NOT NULL
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    filtered.effective_month,
    filtered.separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations
  FROM filtered
  WHERE filtered.separation_category_group IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY filtered.effective_month, filtered.separation_category_group
), combined AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'TOTAL_OCT_NOV_2025' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations
  FROM filtered
  WHERE filtered.separation_category_group IS NOT NULL
), combined_quit AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS effective_month,
    'QUIT' AS separation_category_group,
    COUNT(*) AS separations
  FROM filtered
  WHERE filtered.separation_category_group = 'QUIT'
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month,
  monthly.separation_category_group,
  monthly.separations
FROM monthly
UNION ALL
SELECT
  combined.effective_month,
  combined.separation_category_group,
  combined.separations
FROM combined
UNION ALL
SELECT
  combined_quit.effective_month,
  combined_quit.separation_category_group,
  combined_quit.separations
FROM combined_quit
ORDER BY CASE WHEN effective_month IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, effective_month, separation_category_group
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Compliance Inspection and Support, 1802) average about $74,762 in annualized basic pay, and CBP Officers (1895) average about $104,656. That is a gap of about $29,893, so TSA screeners average about 71% of the CBP Officer figure. Both averages are estimated: pay and location were imputed from job postings for every record with a salary value, not published by OPM. The TSA average covers 42,225 of its 46,913 screener records; the other 4,688 have no salary value at all and are left out.

I read "average salary" as the mean annualized adjusted basic pay for the August 2026 snapshot across all records with a pay value; if you meant the median, or the FY2026 Q1 (October to December 2025) figures, say so.

```sql
SELECT

  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  `location_imputed`,

  COUNT(*) AS `headcount`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_salary`,
```

Verified

Across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), four of the six components are behind plan on hiring and two are ahead. Together they landed 15,861 accessions against 13,285 planned hires, a variance of +2,576 (+19.4%).

The all-DHS total is +2,306, but it also includes 1,779 planned and 1,509 actual hires outside these six components.

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory
889 USAJOBS postings list Border Patrol Agent series 1896 (Customs and Border Protection) in the window from September 2025 to October 2026, counting postings that list several series. The count is of announcements, not openings, and it is an upper bound because postings filled or cancelled before their close date are included.

I read "between September 2025 and October 2026" as postings open at any point in that window (opened on or before October 31, 2026 and closing on or after September 1, 2025). If you meant only postings that opened within those dates, say so and I will rerun it with an opening-date filter.

```sql
WITH `filtered_postings` AS (
  SELECT
    `control_number`,
    `announcement_number`,
    `agency_subelement_code`,
    `agency_subelement`,
    `position_title`,
    `series`,
    `occupational_series_codes`,
    `open_date`,
    `close_date`,
    `opening_status`,
    `total_openings`,
    `total_openings_raw`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `occupational_series_codes` IS NOT NULL
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `control_number` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` <= DATE('2026-10-31')
    AND `close_date` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
),
`posting_count` AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS `posting_count`
  FROM `filtered_postings`
)
SELECT
  `posting_count`.`posting_count`,
  `filtered_postings`.`control_number`,
  `filtered_postings`.`announcement_number`,
  `filtered_postings`.`agency_subelement_code`,
  `filtered_postings`.`agency_subelement`,
  `filtered_postings`.`position_title`,
  `filtered_postings`.`series`,
  `filtered_postings`.`occupational_series_codes`,
  `filtered_postings`.`open_date`,
  `filtered_postings`.`close_date`,
  `filtered_postings`.`opening_status`,
  `filtered_postings`.`total_openings`,
  `filtered_postings`.`total_openings_raw`
FROM `filtered_postings`
CROSS JOIN `posting_count`
ORDER BY `filtered_postings`.`open_date`, `filtered_postings`.`close_date`, `filtered_postings`.`control_number`
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. In the CBP Officer postings announced from September 2025 to October 2026, the higher-grade postings had shorter advertised windows, not longer. Grade 5 postings averaged 29.3 days open and grade 9 averaged 22.4 days, while grades 12 to 15 averaged 5.8 to 7.7 days, with a median of 6 days in every grade from 11 to 15.

| Minimum grade | Postings | Average window (days) | Median window (days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 14 | 29.3 | 30 |
| 9 | 22 | 22.4 | 27 |
| 11 | 1 | 6.0 | 6 |
| 12 | 57 | 7.7 | 6 |
| 13 | 211 | 7.4 | 6 |
| 14 | 126 | 5.8 | 6 |
| 15 | 32 | 6.4 | 6 |

The window is the time from open date to scheduled close date. It is not time to fill, so these figures do not show how long a post stayed unfilled.   FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
```sql
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND (
      `series` = '1895'
      OR array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1895')
    )
    AND `open_date` >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND `open_date` <= DATE '2026-10-31'
    AND `minimum_grade` IS NOT NULL
    AND `minimum_grade` <> '00'
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `close_date` IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT

  AVG(`window_length_days`) AS `average_window_length_days`,

FROM `filtered_postings`

ORDER BY CAST(`minimum_grade` AS INT)
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (CBP, series 1895) retired most in December 2025, with 152 of the 586 retirements in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. The other months ran between 24 and 54 in the autumn and 26 to 52 from January to August.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| Sep 2025 | 54 |
| Oct 2025 | 36 |
| Nov 2025 | 24 |
| Dec 2025 | 152 |
| Jan 2026 | 44 |
| Feb 2026 | 26 |
| Mar 2026 | 31 |
| Apr 2026 | 45 |
| May 2026 | 52 |
| Jun 2026 | 46 |
| Jul 2026 | 45 |
| Aug 2026 | 31 |

These are raw counts, not rates, and the data carries no reason or deferred-resignation flag, so I cannot say whether the December spike is the 2025 deferred resignation wave. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months will grow slightly. I read "in the year" as calendar month of retirement over the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant a rate by month, or all of DHS, say so.

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
),
`retirement_counts` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= TO_DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` ILIKE '%retirement%'
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  `m`.`effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`r`.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`,
  SUM(COALESCE(`r`.`retirement_count`, 0)) OVER () AS `total_retirement_count`
FROM `months` `m`
LEFT JOIN `retirement_counts` `r`
  ON `m`.`effective_month` = `r`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `m`.`effective_month`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. Over the twelve months to August 2026, CBP Officers (HSBD, 1895) in the lower grades (05 to 11) separated at a higher rate than those in the higher grades (12 to 15): 0.049 against 0.032. Grade 12 alone holds about 17,000 of the roughly 27,000 officers, and it sat at 0.032. The lower-grade figure is pulled up mainly by grade 05 (0.102) and grade 07 (0.077).

| Grade | Separation rate, trailing 12 months to Aug 2026 | Separations |
|---|---|---|
| 00 | 0.219 | 7 (mean headcount 32) |
| 05 | 0.102 | 67 |
| 07 | 0.077 | 81 |
| 09 | 0.039 | 61 |
| 11 | 0.007 | 8 |
| 12 | 0.032 | 550 |
| 13 | 0.032 | 136 |
| 14 | 0.038 | 32 |
| 15 | 0.066 | 12 |

Grade 00 and grade 15 rest on very small bases, so treat them as noisy. The 2025 deferred resignation wave contributes no separations in any grade, so the rates with and without it are the same. These grade figures come from a one-off query and are not reconciled to the standard headcount. Late reports keep arriving, so counts will grow.

I read "higher-graded" as grades 12 to 15 against grades 05 to 11, using the trailing twelve-month rate to August 2026, the only window with a rate; if you meant separation counts by grade or a different window, say so.

```sql
WITH `sep_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations_ttm_total`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_drp_wave`,
    SUM(CASE WHEN `drp_indicator` IS NULL OR `drp_indicator` <> 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `separations_ttm_excl_drp`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` ILIKE '%HSBD%'
    AND `occupational_series_code` ILIKE '%1895%'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`hc_2025_09` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_2025_09_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` ILIKE '%HSBD%'
    AND `occupational_series_code` ILIKE '%1895%'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`hc_2026_08` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_2026_08_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` ILIKE '%HSBD%'
    AND `occupational_series_code` ILIKE '%1895%'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `sep_by_grade`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `hc_2025_09`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `hc_2026_08`
)
SELECT
  `g`.`grade`,
  COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) AS `headcount_2025_09_01`,
  COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0) AS `headcount_2026_08_01`,
  CAST(false AS BOOLEAN) AS `grade_imputed`,
  COALESCE(`s`.`separations_ttm_total`, 0) AS `separations_ttm_total`,
  COALESCE(`s`.`separations_drp_wave`, 0) AS `separations_drp_wave`,
  COALESCE(`s`.`separations_ttm_excl_drp`, 0) AS `separations_ttm_excl_drp`,
  try_divide((COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(`s`.`separations_ttm_total`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate_ttm_total`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(`s`.`separations_ttm_excl_drp`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(`h1`.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(`h2`.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate_ttm_excl_drp`
FROM `grades` AS `g`
LEFT JOIN `sep_by_grade` AS `s`
  ON `g`.`grade` = `s`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `hc_2025_09` AS `h1`
  ON `g`.`grade` = `h1`.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `hc_2026_08` AS `h2`
  ON `g`.`grade` = `h2`.`grade`
ORDER BY `g`.`grade`
```

question_text: Which components missed their hiring plan by the most in the first quarter of FY2026?
answer_text:
Verified
Four of the six DHS components landed below their FY2026 Q1 plan (October to December 2025), and FEMA missed by the most: 10 accessions against 681 planned hires, a variance of -671 (-98.5%). TSA was next at -310 (-58.2%), then USCIS at -201 (-50.1%) and CISA at -97 (-96.0%). ICE was far above plan (+5,123, +482.4%), so DHS as a whole landed 8,528 accessions against 4,628 planned hires, +3,900 (+84.3%).

| Component | Planned hires | Accessions | Variance | Variance % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FEMA (HSCB) | 681 | 10 | -671 | -98.5% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 101 | 4 | -97 | -96.0% |
| TSA (HSBC) | 533 | 223 | -310 | -58.2% |
| USCIS (HSAB) | 401 | 200 | -201 | -50.1% |
| CBP (HSBD) | 1,257 | 1,385 | +128 | +10.2% |
| ICE (HSBB) | 1,062 | 6,185 | +5,123 | +482.4% |

These six components account for 4,035 of the 4,628 planned hires and 8,007 of the 8,528 accessions. The remaining 593 planned hires and 521 accessions sit in planned cells I did not break out, so I have not ranked them. Late OPM files keep adding accessions for this quarter, so these shortfalls will narrow. I read "missed by the most" as the largest shortfall in hires against plan for FY2026 Q1, ranked by hires and by percent; if you meant the largest gap in either direction, or separations, say so.

Of these, 702 were quits (372 in October and 330 in November), 126 were retirements, and 21 were transfers out. No termination separations appear for these two months.

The 849 is 261 below the 1,110 figure TSA gave Congress. The data alone does not show why, whether from a different window, a different definition, or a different counting basis, so check how the 1,110 was counted before quoting either number. These months are well past, so late reports should add little. The one-off query returned counts only, with no location fields, so no estimated figures are involved.

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    workforce.semantic.separation.effective_month,
    CASE
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%QUIT%' THEN 'quit'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY%'
        OR workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT%' THEN 'retirement'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%TERMINATION%' THEN 'termination'
      WHEN workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%TRANSFER OUT%' THEN 'transfer out'
    END AS separation_category_group
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE workforce.semantic.separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBC'
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.occupational_series_code = '1802'
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.effective_month IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category IS NOT NULL

      OR workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY%'
      OR workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT%'
      OR workforce.semantic.separation.separation_category ILIKE '%TERMINATION%'

)
```

OPM records show 94 FEMA accessions effective October 2025 through May 2026, against GAO's 134, so the OPM figure is 40 short even if all of May is counted. Adding the monthly rows: October 1, November 8, December 1, January 5, February 0, March 2, April 1, May 76, total 94. The data is month-level only, so the May figure is the whole month, not just through May 15. Through May 15 the OPM count is between 18 (October to April) and 94. Late reports keep arriving, so the count will grow. The data does not show how GAO counted, so the gap may be a definition difference; check that before quoting either figure.

```sql
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    accession.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS accession_count
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`accession` AS accession
  WHERE accession.agency_subelement_code = 'HSCB'
    AND accession.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND accession.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND accession.effective_month <= DATE '2026-05-01'
  GROUP BY accession.effective_month
),
total AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(monthly.accession_count) AS total_accessions

SELECT

  'effective_month is month-level only; counts include full months from 2025-10 through 2026-04, and May 2026 is reported as the full month because day-level filtering through 2026-05-15 is not available' AS note
FROM monthly
CROSS JOIN total
ORDER BY monthly.effective_month
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

As of the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, series 1802) averaged an estimated $74,762 in annualized basic pay across 42,225 people, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) averaged an estimated $104,656 across 27,650. That puts TSA screeners about $29,893 lower, or roughly 40% below CBP Officers.

Every pay figure for both cells is imputed from job postings, not published by OPM, so quote these as estimates. The standard calculations do not carry pay, so this came from a one-off query, which I ran with the following SQL. I read "average salary" as the mean annualized adjusted basic pay in the August 2026 snapshot; if you meant a different period or a median, say so.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_pay`,
  COUNT(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `headcount_used`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `imputed_row_count`,
  CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN true ELSE false END AS `any_pay_imputed`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `annualized_adjusted_basic_pay` IS NOT NULL
  AND ((`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'))
GROUP BY
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  `occupational_series_code`,
  `occupational_series`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`, `occupational_series_code`
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?

Across FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), four components landed behind the staffing plan on hiring and two landed ahead. All of DHS landed 2,306 accessions (15.3%) over plan.

| Transportation Security Administration (HSBC) | 2,368 | 1,336 | -1,032 | -43.6% |

question_text: How many postings listed the Border Patrol series 1896 between September 2025 and October 2026, counting ones that list several series?
answer_text:
Exploratory

889 USAJOBS postings listed Border Patrol series 1896 among their series, with open dates from September 1, 2025 through October 31, 2026. Each posting is counted once, including those that also list other series. The count covers all DHS components, and it includes supervisory and programs titles that list 1896. Postings are announcements, not openings, and the count is an upper bound on what was advertised, since postings filled or cancelled early may still appear.

I read this as all DHS postings that list series 1896 by open date; if you meant only CBP postings or total openings rather than postings, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered_postings AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `control_number`,
    `position_title`,
    `open_date`,
    `close_date`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`job_posting`
  WHERE `control_number` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` IS NOT NULL
    AND `open_date` BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2026-10-31')
    AND array_contains(`occupational_series_codes`, '1896')
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS `posting_count`,
  `position_title`,
  `open_date`,
  `close_date`
FROM `filtered_postings`
ORDER BY `open_date`, `position_title`, `control_number`
```

question_text: Do higher-grade CBP Officer postings stay open longer than lower-grade ones?
answer_text:
Exploratory
No. In the CBP Officer postings opened September 2025 to October 2026, the higher grades closed fastest: grades 12 to 15 had a median of 6 days open, while grade 5 had a median of 30 days and grade 9 a median of 27 days.

| Grade | Postings | Average days open | Median days open |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 14 | 29.3 | 30 |
| 9 | 22 | 22.4 | 27 |
| 12 | 57 | 7.7 | 6 |
| 13 | 211 | 7.4 | 6 |
| 14 | 126 | 5.8 | 6 |
| 15 | 32 | 6.4 | 6 |

Grades 00 (6 postings, median 13 days) and 11 (1 posting, 6 days) are too small to read. These are the scheduled open-to-close windows of the announcements, not time to fill, and the data does not record when a position was actually filled. I read "stay open longer" as the open-to-close length of each announcement by its minimum grade; if you meant how long a vacancy stayed unfilled, that is not in the data.

```sql
SELECT
  job_posting.minimum_grade AS grade,
  COUNT(*) AS number_of_postings,
  AVG(DATEDIFF(job_posting.close_date, job_posting.open_date)) AS avg_days_open,
  PERCENTILE_APPROX(DATEDIFF(job_posting.close_date, job_posting.open_date), 0.5) AS median_days_open
FROM workforce.semantic.job_posting
WHERE job_posting.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
  AND array_contains(job_posting.occupational_series_codes, '1895')
  AND job_posting.open_date >= DATE('2025-09-01')
  AND job_posting.open_date <= DATE('2026-10-31')
  AND job_posting.minimum_grade IS NOT NULL
  AND job_posting.open_date IS NOT NULL
  AND job_posting.close_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY job_posting.minimum_grade
ORDER BY job_posting.minimum_grade
```

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, series 1895) had 552 retirements in the twelve months from September 2025 to August 2026. December 2025 was the peak at 150, about 27% of the year, and November 2025 was the lowest at 23. Outside December, the monthly count ran between 24 and 49.

The one-off query counted only the two retirement categories (voluntary retirement and early out) and did not split out deferred resignation program exits, so I can't confirm whether the December spike is that wave. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months, including August 2026, will grow.

I read "when in the year" as calendar months across the trailing twelve months to August 2026; if you meant a fiscal-year view or retirements excluding the deferred resignation wave, say so.

```sql
WITH months AS (
  SELECT explode(sequence(DATE '2025-09-01', DATE '2026-08-01', INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS effective_month
), retirement_counts AS (
  SELECT
    separation.effective_month,
    COUNT(*) AS retirement_count
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation` AS separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month IS NOT NULL
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.separation_category IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT')
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
  GROUP BY separation.effective_month
), monthly AS (
  SELECT
    months.effective_month,
    COALESCE(retirement_counts.retirement_count, 0) AS retirement_count
  FROM months
  LEFT JOIN retirement_counts
    ON months.effective_month = retirement_counts.effective_month
)
SELECT
  monthly.effective_month,
  monthly.retirement_count,
  SUM(monthly.retirement_count) OVER () AS total_retirement_count
FROM monthly
ORDER BY monthly.effective_month
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

138 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) separated with less than one year of federal service from January to August 2026. That is 138 of 591 CBP Officer separations in the same months. Late reports keep arriving, so this count will grow. The short-service separations were quits (59), other separations (63), expired-appointment terminations (14), and individual transfers out (2); no retirements fell under one year.

I read "this year" as calendar 2026 to date (January to August 2026). If you meant the fiscal year from October 2025, or the trailing twelve months to August 2026, say so and I will rerun it.

```sql
WITH `filtered` AS (
  SELECT
    `separation_category`,
    `length_of_service_years`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No, not in a straight line. Among CBP Officers (HSBD, 1895) on the GS pay plan, the trailing twelve-month separation rate to August 2026 is highest at the lowest grades, drops to its lowest at GS-11, and then holds near 3 to 4 percent through GS-12 to GS-14. GS-15 is higher, at 6.6 percent, but that rests on only 12 separations.

| Grade | Separations | Headcount Sep 2025 to Aug 2026 | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| GS-05 | 67 | 412 to 898 | 10.2% |
| GS-07 | 81 | 863 to 1,234 | 7.7% |
| GS-09 | 61 | 1,429 to 1,661 | 3.9% |
| GS-11 | 8 | 1,125 to 1,270 | 0.7% |
| GS-12 | 550 | 17,520 to 17,130 | 3.2% |
| GS-13 | 136 | 4,251 to 4,375 | 3.2% |
| GS-14 | 32 | 834 to 866 | 3.8% |
| GS-15 | 12 | 174 to 188 | 6.6% |

The eight grades add to 947 separations, an overall rate of about 3.5 percent (947 divided by a mean headcount of about 27,115). The grade rows show no separations marked as deferred resignation program (DRP) wave, so the rates are the same with and without it. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow. The rate uses the average of the September 2025 and August 2026 headcounts, which is a rough denominator for GS-05 and GS-07, where headcount grew sharply over the year.

I read "higher-graded" as GS grade for the trailing twelve-month rate to August 2026; if you meant the count of separations by grade, or grade within tenure band, say so.

```sql
WITH sep_by_grade AS (
  SELECT
    separation.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS separations_including_drp,
    SUM(CASE WHEN separation.drp_indicator <> 'Y' OR separation.drp_indicator IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS separations_excluding_drp
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND separation.pay_plan_code = 'GS'
    AND separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY separation.grade
),
start_headcount AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_start
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code = 'GS'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2025-09-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
end_headcount AS (
  SELECT
    workforce_snapshot.grade AS grade,
    COUNT(*) AS headcount_end
  FROM workforce.semantic.workforce_snapshot
  WHERE workforce_snapshot.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND workforce_snapshot.occupational_series_code = '1895'
    AND workforce_snapshot.pay_plan_code = 'GS'
    AND workforce_snapshot.snapshot_month = DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND workforce_snapshot.grade IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY workforce_snapshot.grade
),
grades AS (
  SELECT sep_by_grade.grade FROM sep_by_grade
  UNION
  SELECT start_headcount.grade FROM start_headcount
  UNION
  SELECT end_headcount.grade FROM end_headcount
)
SELECT
  grades.grade AS grade,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_including_drp, 0) AS separations_including_drp,
  COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_drp, 0) AS separations_excluding_drp,
  COALESCE(start_headcount.headcount_start, 0) AS headcount_start,
  COALESCE(end_headcount.headcount_end, 0) AS headcount_end,
  100 * try_divide(
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_including_drp, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_headcount.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_headcount.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate_including_drp,
  100 * try_divide(
    COALESCE(sep_by_grade.separations_excluding_drp, 0),
    try_divide((COALESCE(start_headcount.headcount_start, 0) + COALESCE(end_headcount.headcount_end, 0)),2.0)
  ) AS separation_rate_excluding_drp
FROM grades
LEFT JOIN sep_by_grade
  ON grades.grade = sep_by_grade.grade
LEFT JOIN start_headcount
  ON grades.grade = start_headcount.grade
LEFT JOIN end_headcount
  ON grades.grade = end_headcount.grade
WHERE grades.grade IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY grades.grade
```

question_text: TSA told Congress about 1,110 screeners left during the October and November 2025 shutdown. What does the OPM data show, and how many of those were quits?
answer_text:
Exploratory
The OPM data shows 828 separations of TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, occupational series 1802) with effective dates in October and November 2025, and 702 of them were quits. By month, October 2025 had 372 quits and 72 retirements, and November 2025 had 330 quits and 54 retirements. No terminations or transfers out appear in those two months.

The 828 is 282 below the 1,110 TSA reported to Congress, and the data does not show why. The separation records carry a category, not a reason, so they cannot say whether the shutdown drove any of these exits. Late corrections are possible but small, so these counts may shift slightly. I read "screeners" as the 1802 series within TSA and the period as the calendar months October and November 2025; if you meant all TSA occupations, say so and I can pull that count.

```sql
WITH categorized AS (
  SELECT
    `separation`.`effective_month`,
    CASE
      WHEN `separation`.`separation_category` = 'QUIT' THEN 'quit'
      WHEN `separation`.`separation_category` IN ('RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY', 'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT') THEN 'retirement'
      WHEN `separation`.`separation_category` = 'TERMINATION' THEN 'termination'
      WHEN `separation`.`separation_category` = 'TRANSFER OUT' THEN 'transfer out'
    END AS `category`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `separation`.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC'
    AND `separation`.`occupational_series_code` = '1802'
    AND `separation`.`effective_month` IN (DATE '2025-10-01', DATE '2025-11-01')
    AND `separation`.`separation_category` IN (
      'QUIT',
      'RETIREMENT - VOLUNTARY',
      'RETIREMENT - EARLY OUT',
      'TERMINATION',
      'TRANSFER OUT'
    )
), monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    `categorized`.`effective_month`,
    `categorized`.`category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM categorized
  WHERE `categorized`.`effective_month` IS NOT NULL
    AND `categorized`.`category` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `categorized`.`effective_month`, `categorized`.`category`
), combined_counts AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
    'total separations' AS `category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM categorized
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CAST(NULL AS DATE) AS `effective_month`,
    'quit' AS `category`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separation_count`
  FROM categorized
  WHERE `categorized`.`category` = 'quit'
```

question_text: What's the average salary of TSA screeners, and how does it compare with CBP Officers?
answer_text:
Exploratory

On the August 2026 snapshot, TSA screeners (Transportation Security Administration, 1802) averaged $74,762 in annualized basic pay across 42,225 people, and CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) averaged $104,656 across 27,650 people, about $29,893 (roughly 40%) more. Every pay value for both groups is imputed: OPM did not publish them, so they were filled in from USAJOBS postings and are estimates, not reported pay. The comparison is only as good as those postings-based estimates.

```sql
SELECT
  `agency_subelement_code`,
  `agency_subelement`,
  AVG(`annualized_adjusted_basic_pay`) AS `average_salary`,
  COUNT(*) AS `headcount_used`,
  SUM(CASE WHEN `pay_imputed` = true THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `pay_imputed_count`
FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND `agency_subelement_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `agency_subelement` IS NOT NULL
  AND `occupational_series_code` IS NOT NULL
  AND `annualized_adjusted_basic_pay` IS NOT NULL
  AND (
    (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBC' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1802')
    OR (`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD' AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895')
  )
GROUP BY `agency_subelement_code`, `agency_subelement`
ORDER BY `agency_subelement_code`
```

question_text: Add up the first three quarters of FY2026: how far behind plan is each component on hiring?

Summed over FY2026 Q1 to Q3 (October 2025 to June 2026), CBP (HSBD) and ICE (HSBB) landed ahead of the plan for accessions, while TSA (HSBC), USCIS (HSAB), CISA (HSCA), and FEMA (HSCB) fell behind.

| USCIS (HSAB) | 1,203 | 1,053 | -150 | -12.5% |
| CISA (HSCA) | 303 | 18 | -285 | -94.1% |
| FEMA (HSCB) | 2,043 | 147 | -1,896 | -92.8% |

ICE's surplus comes almost entirely from October to December 2025 (+5,123 that quarter, then -39 and -697). Late OPM files keep adding accessions, so the gaps will narrow somewhat. The six components together are 13,285 planned against 15,861 actual (+2,576). The other DHS components, which the review does not break out, make up the rest of the plan: 1,779 planned, 1,509 actual, a variance of -270. I read this as the accessions variance (actual minus planned) for each component, summed over the three quarters; if you meant separations, or the gap as a share of the full-year plan, say so.

question_text: When in the year do CBP Officers retire? Show retirements by month.
answer_text:
Exploratory

CBP Officers (CBP, series 1895) retired most in December 2025, with 152 of the 586 retirements in the twelve months to August 2026 (about a quarter). I added the twelve monthly counts to get the 586 total. Retirements ran between 24 and 152 a month, and the data gives the category only, not why people retired. Late reports keep arriving, so the most recent months (July and August 2026) will grow.

| Month | Retirements |
|---|---|
| September 2025 | 54 |
| October 2025 | 36 |
| November 2025 | 24 |
| December 2025 | 152 |
| January 2026 | 44 |
| February 2026 | 26 |
| March 2026 | 31 |
| April 2026 | 45 |
| May 2026 | 52 |
| June 2026 | 46 |
| July 2026 | 45 |
| August 2026 | 31 |

I read "retire" as the retirement separation category for CBP Officers over the twelve effective months September 2025 to August 2026; if you meant all separations or a different window, say so.

The one-off query that ran:

```sql
WITH `months` AS (
  SELECT EXPLODE(SEQUENCE(TO_DATE('2025-09-01'), TO_DATE('2026-08-01'), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)) AS `effective_month`
), `retirements` AS (
  SELECT
    `effective_month`,
    COUNT(*) AS `retirement_count`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `effective_month` BETWEEN TO_DATE('2025-09-01') AND TO_DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `separation_category` IS NOT NULL
    AND `separation_category` ILIKE '%RETIREMENT%'
  GROUP BY `effective_month`
)
SELECT
  `months`.`effective_month`,
  COALESCE(`retirements`.`retirement_count`, 0) AS `retirement_count`
FROM `months`
LEFT JOIN `retirements`
  ON `months`.`effective_month` = `retirements`.`effective_month`
ORDER BY `months`.`effective_month`
```

question_text: How many CBP Officers who left this year had less than one year of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory
162 CBP Officers (Customs and Border Protection, 1895) separated with less than one year of federal service between October 2025 and August 2026 (FY2026 to date), out of 875 separations in that period. Quits (72 of 173) and "other separation" (74 of 133) account for nearly all of them; no retirements or transfers under one year appear. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly. I read "this year" as FY2026 to date; if you meant the trailing twelve months to August 2026, or calendar 2026, say so.

```sql
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT
    separation.separation_category,
    separation.length_of_service_years
  FROM workforce.semantic.separation
  WHERE separation.effective_month >= DATE '2025-10-01'
    AND separation.effective_month <= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND separation.agency_subelement_code = 'HSBD'
    AND separation.occupational_series_code = '1895'
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(filtered.separation_category, 'ALL') AS separation_category,
  SUM(CASE WHEN filtered.length_of_service_years < 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS under_one_year_count,
  COUNT(*) AS total_separations
FROM filtered
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((filtered.separation_category), ())
ORDER BY CASE WHEN COALESCE(filtered.separation_category, 'ALL') = 'ALL' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, separation_category
```

question_text: Are higher-graded CBP Officers leaving at a higher rate than lower grades?
answer_text:
Exploratory

No. CBP Officers in grades 13 to 15 separated at a rate of 0.034 over the twelve months to August 2026, about the same as grades 5 to 12 combined at 0.035. Grade 12, which holds most of the cell, is at 0.032. The high rates sit in the lower grades: grade 05 at 0.102 and grade 07 at 0.077. Grade 15 is at 0.066, but that rests on 181 people. The cell as a whole separated at 0.0351, with or without the 2025 deferred resignation wave, since no wave separations are flagged in this cell for this window. Late reports keep arriving, so these counts will grow slightly. Grades 00 and 11 are small and noisy.

| Grade | Separations | Mean headcount | Separation rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 00 | 7 | 32 | 0.219 |
| 05 | 67 | 655 | 0.102 |
| 07 | 81 | 1,049 | 0.077 |
| 09 | 61 | 1,545 | 0.039 |
| 11 | 8 | 1,198 | 0.007 |
| 12 | 550 | 17,325 | 0.032 |
| 13 | 136 | 4,313 | 0.032 |
| 14 | 32 | 850 | 0.038 |
| 15 | 12 | 181 | 0.066 |

I read "higher-graded" as grades 13 to 15 against the lower grades, using the separation rate over the trailing twelve months to August 2026. If you meant separation counts, or a different grade cut such as grade 12 and above, say so.

The grade breakdown came from this query:

```sql
WITH `start_choice` AS (
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN EXISTS (
             SELECT 1
             FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
             WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-08-01')
               AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
               AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
               AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
           ) THEN DATE('2025-08-01')
           ELSE DATE('2025-09-01')
         END AS `start_snapshot_used`
),
`sep` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`start_hc` AS (
  SELECT
    ws.`grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_start`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot` ws
  CROSS JOIN `start_choice` sc
  WHERE ws.`agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND ws.`occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND ws.`snapshot_month` = sc.`start_snapshot_used`
    AND ws.`grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ws.`grade`
),
`end_hc` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_end`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grades` AS (
  SELECT `grade` FROM `sep`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `start_hc`
  UNION
  SELECT `grade` FROM `end_hc`
)
SELECT
  g.`grade`,
  COALESCE(s.`separations`, 0) AS `separations`,
  COALESCE(sh.`headcount_start`, 0) AS `headcount_start`,
  COALESCE(eh.`headcount_end`, 0) AS `headcount_end`,
  try_divide((COALESCE(sh.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(eh.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`,
  CASE
    WHEN (COALESCE(sh.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(eh.`headcount_end`, 0)) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE try_divide(COALESCE(s.`separations`, 0),(try_divide((COALESCE(sh.`headcount_start`, 0) + COALESCE(eh.`headcount_end`, 0)),2.0)))
  END AS `separation_rate`,
  sc.`start_snapshot_used`
FROM `grades` g
LEFT JOIN `sep` s
  ON g.`grade` = s.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `start_hc` sh
  ON g.`grade` = sh.`grade`
LEFT JOIN `end_hc` eh
  ON g.`grade` = eh.`grade`
CROSS JOIN `start_choice` sc
ORDER BY g.`grade`
```

The deferred-resignation check came from this query:

```sql
WITH `sep_by_grade` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `separations`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`separation`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `effective_month` >= DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `effective_month` <= DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `drp_indicator` <> 'Y'
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`hc_2025_09` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_2025_09_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2025-09-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`hc_2026_08` AS (
  SELECT
    `grade`,
    COUNT(*) AS `headcount_2026_08_01`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
    AND `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `grade` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `grade`
),
`grade_metrics` AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(s.`grade`, h1.`grade`, h2.`grade`) AS `grade`,
    COALESCE(s.`separations`, 0) AS `separations`,
    COALESCE(h1.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) AS `headcount_2025_09_01`,
    COALESCE(h2.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0) AS `headcount_2026_08_01`,
    try_divide((COALESCE(h1.`headcount_2025_09_01`, 0) + COALESCE(h2.`headcount_2026_08_01`, 0)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`
  FROM `sep_by_grade` s
  FULL OUTER JOIN `hc_2025_09` h1
    ON s.`grade` = h1.`grade`
  FULL OUTER JOIN `hc_2026_08` h2
    ON COALESCE(s.`grade`, h1.`grade`) = h2.`grade`
)
SELECT
  `grade`,
  `separations`,
  `headcount_2025_09_01`,
  `headcount_2026_08_01`,
  `mean_headcount`,
  try_divide(`separations`,NULLIF(`mean_headcount`, 0)) AS `separation_rate`,
  'drp_indicator' AS `drp_exclusion_field_used`
FROM `grade_metrics`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'TOTAL' AS `grade`,
  SUM(`separations`) AS `separations`,
  SUM(`headcount_2025_09_01`) AS `headcount_2025_09_01`,
  SUM(`headcount_2026_08_01`) AS `headcount_2026_08_01`,
  try_divide((SUM(`headcount_2025_09_01`) + SUM(`headcount_2026_08_01`)),2.0) AS `mean_headcount`,
  try_divide(SUM(`separations`),NULLIF(try_divide((SUM(`headcount_2025_09_01`) + SUM(`headcount_2026_08_01`)),2.0), 0)) AS `separation_rate`,
  'drp_indicator' AS `drp_exclusion_field_used`
FROM `grade_metrics`
ORDER BY CASE WHEN `grade` = 'TOTAL' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, `grade`
```

question_text: Roughly how many CBP Officers could retire in the next five years, going by age bracket and years of service?
answer_text:
Exploratory

The age field is empty for CBP Officers in the August 2026 snapshot, so I cannot break retirement eligibility down by age bracket. On years of service alone, 8,732 of 27,650 CBP Officers (31.6%) had 20 or more years at August 2026, and a further 8,773 (31.7%) had 10 to 20 years. The records do not split the 10-to-20 group further, so I cannot give a five-year retirement count; the 8,732 is a floor for officers already at 20 years, not a forecast. Using the separation categories for retirements over the past twelve months would show how many officers actually left by retirement. Late reports keep arriving, so recent counts will grow.

The one-off query that checked for age returned no rows:

```sql
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%UNDER 30%' THEN 'under 30'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%30 TO 39%' THEN '30 to 39'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%40 TO 49%' THEN '40 to 49'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%50 TO 54%' THEN '50 to 54'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%55 TO 59%' THEN '55 to 59'
      WHEN `age_bracket` ILIKE '%60 AND OVER%' OR `age_bracket` ILIKE '%60 OR OVER%' OR `age_bracket` ILIKE '%60 OVER%' THEN '60 and over'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `age_bucket`,
    CASE
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` < 1 THEN 'under 1'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 1 AND `length_of_service_years` < 3 THEN '1-3'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 3 AND `length_of_service_years` < 5 THEN '3-5'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 5 AND `length_of_service_years` < 10 THEN '5-10'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 10 AND `length_of_service_years` < 20 THEN '10-20'
      WHEN `length_of_service_years` >= 20 THEN '20+'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS `service_bucket`
  FROM `workforce`.`semantic`.`workforce_snapshot`
  WHERE `snapshot_month` = DATE('2026-08-01')
    AND `source_file` = 'employment_202608_1.parquet'
    AND `agency_subelement_code` = 'HSBD'
    AND `occupational_series_code` = '1895'
), counts AS (
  SELECT
    `age_bucket`,
    `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `employee_count`
  FROM base
  WHERE `age_bucket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY `age_bucket`, `service_bucket`
), total_row AS (
  SELECT
    'Total' AS `age_bucket`,
    'Total' AS `service_bucket`,
    COUNT(*) AS `employee_count`
  FROM base
  WHERE `age_bucket` IS NOT NULL
    AND `service_bucket` IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT `age_bucket`, `service_bucket`, `employee_count`
FROM counts
UNION ALL
SELECT `age_bucket`, `service_bucket`, `employee_count`
FROM total_row
ORDER BY
  CASE `age_bucket`
    WHEN 'under 30' THEN 1
    WHEN '30 to 39' THEN 2
    WHEN '40 to 49' THEN 3
    WHEN '50 to 54' THEN 4
    WHEN '55 to 59' THEN 5
    WHEN '60 and over' THEN 6
    WHEN 'Total' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END,
  CASE `service_bucket`
    WHEN 'under 1' THEN 1
    WHEN '1-3' THEN 2
    WHEN '3-5' THEN 3
    WHEN '5-10' THEN 4
    WHEN '10-20' THEN 5
    WHEN '20+' THEN 6
    WHEN 'Total' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END
```
